title: POC Weekly Sync - Reliability Incident Follow-up
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on last week's reliability incidents (intermittent timeouts, spikes in 5xxs, and rate-limit throttling). Redwood SE walked through logs, identified hotspots (KV cache invalidation, NLB timeouts, retry storm), and proposed mitigations including request pacing, dedicated burst nodes, and config tweaks. Agreed action items and timeline for a follow-up test and post-mortem.
next_steps: Priya to share aggregated error logs and trace links by 2025-03-14
Acme to run repro script in staging and report success rate by 2025-03-17
Alex to open a Dedicated burst evaluation quote and share by 2025-03-19
Schedule incident post-mortem with infra and SREs the week of 2025-03-17
action_items: Priya Patel (SE) - provide aggregated request+5xx logs and span traces (due 2025-03-14)
Tara Singh (SRE) - run repro script and collect curl level traces in staging (due 2025-03-17)
Alex Chen (AE) - share Dedicated burst cost estimate and trial terms (due 2025-03-19)
Brian Wu (ML Eng) - test client-side retry/backoff config and report metrics (due 2025-03-17)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Rao (Redwood Support), Jenna Morales (Acme Eng Manager), Brian Wu (Acme ML Eng), Tara Singh (Acme SRE)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Okay folks thanks for joining, 15:00 UTC, we'll run 45 minutes. Quick roll call, say hi.
[00:12] Jenna Morales: Hey Alex, Jenna here.
[00:15] Brian Wu: Brian.
[00:17] Tara Singh: Tara.
[00:19] Priya Patel: Priya from Redwood.
[00:22] Alex Chen: Samir?
[00:23] Samir Rao: Samir on support.
[00:25] Alex Chen: Great. Agenda: incident recap, what we found in logs, proposed mitigations (rate limiting, retries, dedicated nodes), and next steps. Priya, want to kick off with the incident timeline?

[00:40] Priya Patel: Sure. So recap — last Thursday between 02:10 and 02:35 UTC you hit an elevated 5xx rate, plus a handful of client-observed timeouts. From our side we saw a correlation with sudden traffic bursts from a batch job hitting the inference endpoint, which pushed concurrent streams up by about 3x vs baseline. That triggered our autoscaler to start spinning up additional workers but there was a short window where the NLB started dropping connections and we saw a retry storm from the client.

[01:15] Brian Wu: Quick q - are those client retries coming from our side or from Redwood's SDK? We saw a lot of 429s then 5xx. Some of it looks like our app did aggressive retries.

[01:28] Priya Patel: Good point. We instrumented both sides. There's evidence of retries at the client, and some gateway-level retries. Also we saw KV cache misses on the second warmup phase which added CPU pressure on the hosts. So multiple factors: spike, cache invalidation, and retry amplification.

[02:00] Tara Singh: The 5xx codes - are they all 500s or do you have more granular codes? We saw 502/504s at our LB.

[02:12] Priya Patel: Mix: mostly 503/504 from the NLB layer and 5xx from the runtime (OOM-ish in a few cases). A couple of 502s when the gateway couldn't handshake to a new worker.

[02:32] Jenna Morales: Any chance this is due to our model size changing? We rolled a quantized version two weeks ago.

[02:39] Priya Patel: We checked the model variant — the quantized version behaves similarly in perf, but it does have a slightly higher memory footprint for KV cache fills under heavy concurrency. Not enough to explain full outage, but it contributed.

[03:05] Alex Chen: On client-side we recommended progressive backoff but I know the app uses a naive immediate retry on failure. Brian, is that something you can change quickly?

[03:15] Brian Wu: Yeah we can do exponential backoff and jitter, but we want to avoid changing behavior that hides problems. We can implement a short-term fix for the POC.

[03:30] Priya Patel: Another mitigation is request pacing on the Redwood side via a token-bucket limiter or route-level concurrency cap; we can add a soft queue to smooth bursts. That prevents the NLB from getting thrashed and buys time for autoscale.

[03:50] Tara Singh: How does that interact with SLOs? If you queue, some requests will see higher p95 latency.

[03:58] Priya Patel: Right, it's a tradeoff - slightly higher tail latency vs fewer timeouts and fewer 5xx errors. For the POC we suggested a soft cap that keeps p99 within acceptable range but reduces 5xx. We can tune.

[04:20] Alex Chen: We also looked at rate-limits. Your current plan is the hosted tier with shared capacity; the spikes can cause you to hit per-minute rate limits which lead to 429s. One intermediate step is to enable a short-term Dedicated burst or reserve a small Dedicated pool for heavy batch windows.

[04:40] Jenna Morales: Can you quantify costs for that burst option? We need ballpark before we ask finance.

[04:46] Alex Chen: I'll send a cost estimate today — sample quote for a 2x burst capacity window reserved for 4 hours/day. I can include options: fixed reservation vs overage pricing.

[05:03] Priya Patel: I want to point out we found a repeatable repro scenario. We shared a small repro script in the shared notes earlier (link: https://redwood.app/poc/acme/repro-logs). The script steps up concurrency quickly and reproduces the 5xxs within ~2 minutes. That will help you test client-side changes.

[05:28] Brian Wu: Received. We'll run it in staging. If we throttle our client retries we saw the median success rate improve during our quick runs.

[05:40] Tara Singh: Regarding logs — what traces did you pull? We prefer having full-span traces to tie to our APM.

[05:47] Priya Patel: We exported aggregated spans from our tracer (trace ids included) and attached the high-level flame graphs. I'll share the consolidated logs as a single tarball and a GCP/Datadog link. Expect that by Friday.

[06:05] Jenna Morales: Cool. On the NLB side we saw connection resets around 02:12 - is that consistent with your time?

[06:11] Priya Patel: Yes, that's the exact window. We suspect the autoscaler was firing up new nodes and the NLB health checks briefly marked targets unhealthy during warm attach. We're going to change the attach flow to pre-warm some worker capacity in the next rollout.

[06:31] Alex Chen: Samir, did support find anything else residual?

[06:34] Samir Rao: We traced a couple of hosts that hit high GC and then had the runtime restart. On two hosts the model allocator got into thrash due to concurrent large KV cache fills; we are adding a cap on concurrent cache loads. Also we've improved the health check behavior so new hosts don't get traffic until they've fully loaded weights.

[07:00] Brian Wu: That cap on cache loads — could that increase latency? If you cap cache loads, first requests might be slower.

[07:08] Priya Patel: Yes initial requests will see slightly higher latency; but it avoids multi-host OOMs and 5xx cascades. Again tradeoff. For the POC we can try a conservative cap.

[07:25] Jenna Morales: One other thing: we saw some spikes in requests coming from an internal cron at 02:00. We can reschedule - but that requires coordination.

[07:34] Tara Singh: We'll do that as a short-term fix. But I'd rather not rely only on scheduling; we need graceful degradation too.

[07:42] Alex Chen: Agreed. So summary of recommended mitigations: client-side retry/backoff, request pacing/token-bucket on Redwood, cap concurrent KV cache fills, pre-warm Dedicated workers / change attach flow, and consider Dedicated burst for heavy windows.

[08:05] Priya Patel: Also a note on rate limits — some 429s were from hitting per-route TPS buckets; we can temporarily bump limits for your account during the POC if you want. That requires an internal config change but is doable.

[08:22] Jenna Morales: Bumping limits temporarily sounds useful so we can test without hitting hard 429s.

[08:28] Alex Chen: We'll do that as a low-friction step. I'll coordinate.

[08:33] Brian Wu: For measurement — what metrics should we send back after we run the repro? Success rate, median/p95/p99 latency, and rate of 5xx/429? Anything else?

[08:43] Priya Patel: Also include client retry counts, concurrency over time, and any dropped connections seen at the LB. If you can capture a few full traces for failed requests that helps a lot.

[09:00] Tara Singh: On the SSO/security side — unrelated but FYI, we'll need SOC2 docs for any Dedicated trial. Jenna will coordinate.

[09:08] Jenna Morales: Yep we'll want that before any Dedicated purchase.

[09:12] Alex Chen: No problem, I'll attach the SOC2 and KMS integration notes in the follow-up email.

[09:20] Priya Patel: Small gotcha we noticed — the client's SDK version was an older release that didn't support connection pooling improvements. Upgrading to v1.4.2 reduces socket churn. Brian, can you try that in staging?

[09:33] Brian Wu: Yes we'll bump SDK and report.

[09:36] Jenna Morales: Any immediate blocker on Redwood's side we should know about for the fix rollout?

[09:41] Samir Rao: No blockers, we can push the cache-cap and health-check change to a canary pool tomorrow, monitor for regressions, then roll to all.

[09:52] Alex Chen: Cool. Let's go through action items and owners now. Priya will share logs/traces; Tara/Brian will run repro and test client changes; Alex will send cost quote and bump limits; Samir will deploy the health-check + cache cap canary. Any objections?

[10:15] Jenna Morales: All good. One question: timeline for the post-mortem?

[10:19] Alex Chen: Tentatively week of 2025-03-17. We'll coordinate with your infra folks to join.

[10:25] Brian Wu: One more practical ask - can you provide a short runbook for diagnosing these sorts of incidents? Even a 1-pager.

[10:33] Priya Patel: Yes, we'll prepare a 1-page incident runbook: quick checks, key metrics, and repro steps. We'll link it to the shared doc.

[10:44] Jenna Morales: Great. Anything else?

[10:47] Tara Singh: Not from SRE.

[10:50] Alex Chen: Alright team, thanks for the quick turnaround. We'll follow up with the artifacts and next steps.

[10:57] Priya Patel: I'll upload the aggregated logs to the shared folder and ping everyone.

[11:02] Alex Chen: Meeting adjourned.

References:
- repro script: https://redwood.app/poc/acme/repro-logs
- support notes: https://redwood.app/poc/acme/support-20250312

End of transcript.
